objectives.text: Authorize Federal Reserve banks, under Board-prescribed rules, to make secured advances to member banks on short-maturity time or demand notes, and on longer-maturity time notes secured by one-to-four family residential mortgage loans.

citations.quote: Any Federal Reserve bank, under rules and regulations prescribed by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, may make advances to any member bank on its time or demand notes having maturities of not more than four months and which are secured to the satisfaction of such Federal Reserve bank.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, any Federal Reserve bank, under rules and regulations prescribed by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, may make advances to any member bank on its time notes having such maturities as the Board may prescribe and which are secured by mortgage loans covering a one-to-four family residence.

objectives.text: Constrain the duration and consequences of Federal Reserve advances to undercapitalized and critically undercapitalized depository institutions, coupling continued lending to viability certification and imposing loss-liability and reporting consequences on the Board — structural features bearing on how discount-window access to weak institutions is gated and monitored.

citations.quote: Except as provided in paragraph (2), no advances to any undercapitalized depository institution by any Federal Reserve bank under this section may be outstanding for more than 60 days in any 120-day period.

definitions.definition: A depository institution is "viable" if the Board or the appropriate Federal banking agency determines, giving due regard to the economic conditions and circumstances in the market in which the institution operates, that the institution (i) is not critically undercapitalized; (ii) is not expected to become critically undercapitalized; and (iii) is not expected to be placed in conservatorship or receivership.

notes: This source is the raw statutory text of 12 U.S.C. 347b (Federal Reserve Act s.10B), governing Federal Reserve bank advances to individual member banks, including special time limits, viability-certification mechanics, and Board loss-liability/reporting duties for advances to undercapitalized/critically undercapitalized institutions. The source text contains no explicit discussion of FHLB collateral/operational rules, discount-window stigma, Call Report or FR 2052a reporting timing/granularity, or the Hsu/McKernan reform proposals named in the ratified scope; it is included here strictly as binding statutory authority underlying the discount-window mechanics (differential treatment of weak institutions, certification gating, Board liability/reporting) that bear on the program's diagnostic mapping of discount-window structure and potential stigma sources. No harmonization, paraphrase, or interpretive gloss has been applied; ambiguities and internal structure (e.g., the negative-obligation phrasing in (b)(4), and the layered certification/exception scheme in (b)(2)-(3)) are preserved as written. All editorial/amendment/effective-date material outside the operative text of s.10B itself was excluded as non-operative history, consistent with the ratified scope's focus on the current regime.
